title: Recipe
description: A chaotic, one-pot vegan chili made from whatever you can find in the back of your pantry. It's a testament to survival, resourcefulness, and the fact that you really need to go grocery shopping. Surprisingly delicious.
name: Kitchen Catastrophe Chili

wet.name: Vegetable broth
wet.notes: or water from a hopefully safe source

dry.name: Chili powder
dry.notes: the dusty one from the back

other.name: Garlic
other.notes: cloves, minced or smashed in a panic

other.name: Bell pepper
other.notes: any color, looking a bit wrinkly, chopped

instructions: Forage for your ingredients in the wilds of your pantry and refrigerator. Chop the onion, bell pepper, and garlic with the urgency of a survivor. Don't aim for perfection.
Heat the oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Throw in the onion and bell pepper and cook until they soften, about 5-7 minutes. A little charring adds character.
Add the frantically minced garlic and cook for another minute until you can smell it. This is your signal that things are about to get serious.
Dump in the chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Stir it all together for about 30 seconds, creating a fragrant cloud of dust, a ghost of spices past.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and vegetable broth, scraping the bottom of the pot to unstick any flavorful casualties.
Rinse your canned beans and corn as if you're decontaminating them. Add them to the pot. Bring the whole mess to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Let the chili simmer, partially covered, for at least 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally. The longer it simmers, the more the desperate flavors will meld into something coherent.
Season with salt and pepper until it tastes less like a disaster and more like a deliberate meal. Serve hot in whatever clean-ish bowls you can find.
notes: This recipe is a blueprint for chaos. Any beans will do. Got a can of lentils? In they go. Found a sad-looking zucchini? Chop it up and add it. There are no rules when you're cooking to survive... the week.
